title: The Warning Beneath the Ground
intro: Imagine standing beside a deep excavation as voices rise from below and the world above falls silent. The Qur’an preserves this scene as a warning: a community rejects what the messengers bring, punishment closes in, and even its roar becomes part of the testimony. Which collective speaks through those verses?
clues: We are remembered in the Qur’an as a collective defined by one shared fate rather than by an individual name.
We rejected the message brought by messengers, even though what they said was true.
Our remembered identity is tied to a deep cut in the earth, and that feature became part of our name.
On the appointed day, we were brought out and dragged toward the fire.
We could not defend ourselves against the punishment, and we could not hear its roar.
Our faces would be turned in the fire, and we would be driven into it; when questioned, we would say that we were among those who could not respond.
